Letter From NORML Board Member Praising Change in Canada’s Marijuana Policies
Published In The Very Prohibitionist Wall Street Journal

(Marijuananews note: Paul Kuhn is an old friend and a member of the NORML Board.

What is especially important about this letter is that it will be the first time that most people in DEAland will have heard about the developments in Canada. It is astonishing the degree to which even the DEAland elites are kept in the dark about the realties of marijuana prohibition.

The usual prohibitionist propaganda and media blackout on moves away from marijuana prohibition in other countries keeps Americans unaware of what is happening elsewhere.

See
Foreign Affairs Pushes The Party Line At the Highest Levels:
Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda for the Elites.
April's Reefer Madness Award Winner

This letter is a coup in piercing the narc curtain.)

June 25, 1999
From The Wall Street Journal
By Paul H. Kuhn

The usual prohibitionist propaganda and media blackout on moves away from marijuana prohibition in other countries keeps Americans unaware of what is happening elsewhere.

See
Foreign Affairs Pushes The Party Line At the Highest Levels:
Anti-Dutch Prohibitionist Propaganda for the Elites.
April's Reefer Madness Award Winner

This letter is a coup in piercing the narc curtain.)

CANADA MAY BE GOING TO POT

In regard to your June 10 Asides "Canada Shows the Way":

You’re right. Canada is showing the way—on more than just taxes. In April, for example, the Canadian Association of Chiefs of Police came out in favor of decriminalizing minor marijuana offenses. In May, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police said they "fully support" the chiefs’ position.
See
Canadian Police Chiefs To Support "Decriminalization" Of Marijuana.
"Government will give serious consideration to recommendation." -- 2 Stories

Then, Canada’s House of Commons passed (by an overwhelming 204-20 margin) a motion urging the government to "take steps" to approve medical marijuana.
See
Canadian House Of Commons Votes 204 to 29 To Urge The Health Ministry
To "Take Steps" Toward Legalizing Marijuana For Medical Use.
Bloc Quebecois Seeks to Keep Pressure On Health Minister.

And last week, the Health Minister issued guidelines for a series of medical marijuana clinical trials as well as plans to grow and import marijuana for medical purposes—after authorizing two patients to grow and possess their own pot.
See
Canadian Health Minister Issues Call To All Pot Growers To Send Him Their Resumes.
In The Meantime, He Is Going To Try To Get Marijuana From DEAland.
Maybe He Will Have Better Luck Than Our Own Researchers.
Two AIDS Patients Get Exemptions.

Maybe Canada, not California, is becoming the bellwether of change.

Paul H. Kuhn
Nashville, Tenn.
